# Conclusions {#sec-article-05-conclusions}

Receptor-based regionalization added spatial information to the existing attainment-oriented assessment of Congonhas. Quintiles, concentration-profile groups and local spatial association provided complementary descriptions, while source-group attribution connected the selected receiving regions to the simulated contributing activities. The procedure preserved all zoning identifiers and expressed their internal heterogeneity through area shares.

The analysis also demonstrated limits that matter for the proposed public application. Local boundaries depended on neighbourhood choice, emission–concentration splits retained substantial unexplained variation, and the cadastral geometry contained near-zero-area fragments. These findings favour an auditable set of analyses and sensitivities rather than a single unqualified severity label. Final consolidation requires checking source timing, meteorological behaviour, residential support and revised simulation results. The current contribution is a reproducible framework and a quantified exploratory diagnosis, not evidence that the underlying model bias has been corrected.
